questions.stem: In the Hausa-Fulani emirate system, the alkali was the

options.text: commander of the cavalry
Islamic judge who administered Sharia
village age-grade leader
head of the Oyo Mesi

questions.explanation: Alkali courts applied Islamic law in the emirates. The emir was the political and religious head; hakimai were district heads; the madawaki commanded the cavalry. Confusing alkali with any of those offices, or with Yoruba titles, is a common error.

distractorRationale.a: The cavalry commander was the madawaki
distractorRationale.c: Age grades belong to Igbo (and some other) village organisation, not to the emirate judiciary
distractorRationale.d: The Oyo Mesi was the Yoruba council of state in Oyo, headed by the Bashorun

questions.stem: The Oyo Mesi could force an Alaafin to commit suicide. This power is evidence that Oyo's system was

options.text: an absolute theocracy with no checks on the ruler
a centralised monarchy in which the king was nonetheless checked by a council
an acephalous village democracy without a king
a military dictatorship headed by the Are-Ona-Kakanfo

questions.explanation: Oyo had a king — the Alaafin — so it was centralised and monarchical. The Oyo Mesi, headed by the Bashorun, advised him and could reject him by presenting an empty calabash, after which custom required suicide. That is a strong check, not the absence of a king, and not rule by the army commander.

distractorRationale.a: A ruler who can be rejected is not unchecked; nor was Oyo primarily a theocracy in the Sokoto sense
distractorRationale.c: Acephalous organisation describes most Igbo communities, which had no Alaafin
distractorRationale.d: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo commanded the army and was kept outside the capital so that he would not seize the throne

questions.stem: Pre-colonial Igbo political organisation is generally described as acephalous because

options.text: every village was ruled by an emir appointed from Sokoto
there was, in most communities, no single king; power was shared among elders, age grades and titled men
the Oba of Benin appointed all Igbo chiefs
a written constitution named a president of Igboland

questions.explanation: Acephalous means 'without a head' in the sense of no single monarch. Igbo village democracy worked through the assembly, lineage elders, age grades, ozo title-holders and oracles. There were exceptions such as Onitsha and Nri, but the general exam description remains village-based and kingless.

distractorRationale.a: Emirs belong to the Hausa-Fulani system, not to Igbo villages
distractorRationale.c: Benin's Oba did not appoint the political heads of Igbo village republics
distractorRationale.d: Pre-colonial Igbo government was customary, not a written presidential constitution

questions.stem: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo in the Oyo Empire was the

options.text: Islamic judge of the empire
commander of the army, required to live outside the capital
head of the village age grade
district head who collected jangali

questions.explanation: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo was Oyo's field commander. Custom required him to reside outside the capital so that he could not easily overthrow the Alaafin, and tradition held that he must win his wars or take his own life. The office is a favourite identification question.

distractorRationale.a: Islamic judges (alkali) belong to the emirate system
distractorRationale.c: Age grades are an Igbo (and some other) institution
distractorRationale.d: District heads (hakimai) and jangali cattle tax belong to the Hausa-Fulani emirates

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly contrasts the Hausa-Fulani emirate with Igbo village government?

options.text: Both were acephalous systems without officials
The emirate was centralised and hierarchical; Igbo government was generally acephalous and village-based
Igbo communities were ruled by emirs, while Hausa cities had only age grades
Both operated written constitutions modelled on the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: The emirate had a single head, appointed district officials and alkali courts — a pyramid. Igbo political life, in the general case, spread authority among lineages, age grades and titled men with no king at the top. That contrast later explained why indirect rule found chiefs in the North and had to invent warrant chiefs in the East.

distractorRationale.a: The emirate was the opposite of acephalous
distractorRationale.d: Neither system used a modern written constitution

questions.stem: The Hausa-Fulani emirate system that colonial officials met was largely a product of the Sokoto Jihad led by Usman dan Fodio in 1804.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Hausa city-states existed before 1804, but the emirate structure — emirs under the Sultan of Sokoto, Sharia courts, and a Fulani-led ruling class in most emirates — was shaped by the jihad of Usman dan Fodio. That is the system Lugard's indirect rule later used.

distractorRationale.b: Denying the jihad's role confuses the older Hausa kingdoms with the nineteenth-century caliphate order
